$comment: Compound V hooks. SubagentStop was removed in v0.1.1 on the premise that it was undocumented. That premise was WRONG (verified 2026-07-25): Stop and SubagentStop are both documented, exit 2 / decision:block prevents the turn from ending, and Anthropic's own ralph-loop plugin ships a Stop hook. v2.18 RESTORES a blocking Stop hook (epic-goal-stop.sh). SessionStart matcher pattern copied from upstream obra/superpowers v5.1.0. memory-refresh.sh (v2.0) is APPENDED to both events — it is silent (emits no context) and self-backgrounds an FTS5-only `refresh --quick`, so it composes with the banner/nudge without blocking and never installs/downloads. brainstorm-trigger0-nudge.sh (v2.8) uses PreToolUse additionalContext — live-probed 2026-07-11 on Claude Code 2.1.197 (see the probe comment in that hook); reminder only, never blocks.
$comment_stop: Stop takes NO matcher — it is not a tool event. The `|| true` suffix is MECHANISM (a) of the two-part fail-open contract: a non-zero exit from a Stop hook IS a block, and a syntax error in the script is fatal before any in-script trap can run, so the registration itself must neutralize it. MECHANISM (b) lives inside epic-goal-stop.sh (an unconditional-exit-0 EXIT trap plus output suppression on a failed run). Both are required; neither is sufficient. Do NOT remove the `|| true` — see tests/test-epic-goal-stop.sh, which asserts it is present and proves the raw script really does exit non-zero when broken.
$comment_lane_guard: PreToolUse lane-guard (v3.0 Feature E) is registered WITHOUT a `|| true` suffix, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. A non-zero PreToolUse exit is NOT a deny -- it is a non-blocking error whose stderr is shown to the user -- so `|| true` buys nothing here, while lane-guard.sh's own wrapper already discards non-JSON output and exits 0 unconditionally. Copying the Stop idiom would be cargo-culting a mechanism that does not apply. The matcher is `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash`: `Bash` is in the list because the 1D probe (0982ce0) showed a Write|Edit-only matcher is decorative in an environment that nudges agents toward sed/heredocs, and the hook's own header is explicit that shell-command inspection is a supplement -- the git-derived scope gate remains the authority.
$comment_native_points: UserPromptSubmit + PostCompact (v3.0, task-16) close two rows of docs/superpowers/architecture/native-mechanisms.md. UserPromptSubmit is the native "a change request arrived" event -- the activation surface the sizing engine never had, which is why it has run zero times; triage-prompt-nudge.sh is a REMINDER that never writes or commits a record, and fires only when no active run and no covering triage record exist. It carries `|| true` for the same reason the Stop hook does, and a sharper one: UserPromptSubmit is blocking-capable and exit 2 REJECTS THE USER'S PROMPT, which is exactly what bash returns for a parse error above the in-script trap. PostCompact receives the compaction summary (SessionStart does not), so postcompact-resume.sh reuses `compound-v-dashboard.py resume` and reports whether the summary carried the active run ids; in Claude Code 2.1.238 its stdout becomes the compaction's display text, NOT model context, so it complements the v2.19 SessionStart banner rather than replacing it. `timeout: 10` bounds both: they run on every prompt / every compaction and must never be the reason a turn stalls.
